answer.evidence: The podium body is 16px wide from row 7. Rows 7-12 are a tan top surface (#bc9250) with scuffs. Row 13 is a lighter front-edge line (#cba76c), and rows 14-15 are darker eave shadow (#96623a, #533020). Rows 16-31 are a vertical front face with a recessed panel, an emblem and a base molding, which makes 16 front-face rows. The dark monitor and mic arm above row 7 stand on the top and count as decor. The top is 6 rows deep, more than a 1-2 row rim, so it reads like the green cabinet reference (top plus edge plus eave).

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small podium: a wooden body with a crest panel and a dark lectern top. It has 9 visible tones per 16x16 tile, equal to the hedge reference (9). That is below the stall (17) and well (20), but those are much larger, more complex props. Near-flat coverage is 0%, so there are no big flat fills, and the body and crest panel show tonal variation. Only 24% of dark edge pixels are near-neutral, so the outline mostly leans tinted brown rather than being a uniform black sticker line. It has about 4 wood and gold steps against roughly 5 on the references, which is slightly shallow. Its total of 13 colours is in line with the bench and lamp (14 each). A careful artist would probably accept it next to the bench and hedge without it looking noticeably flatter, though it is a little less rich than the stall and well.

The references use 5-6. The measured facts support it: 9 visible tones per tile matches the hedge (9) and is below the stall (17) and well (20). Near-flat coverage is 0%, and there are no 5x5 single-colour blocks, so it has no flat fills. Only 24% of dark edge pixels are near-neutral, so the outline mostly leans brown, like the wood-adjacent outlines on the references, and is not a uniform black sticker line. Texture comes from the emblem and the panel edge/grain variation. It is somewhat less textured than the stall and well, but about on par with the bench and hedge, the closest kinds. The total of 13 distinct colours is low next to the larger props, but similar to the bench (14) and lamp (14) at this size. It is slightly thinner than the best references, but a careful artist would accept it beside them.
